resources.string: FTC Reconnect
COOKIE CODERS / FTC CONNECTION HELPER
Fix the FTC connection
This phone: %1$s\nRobot Controller: %2$s
DEVICE NAMES
Driver Station Wi-Fi Direct name
Robot Controller Wi-Fi Direct name

Enter the exact, case-sensitive names shown in the FTC apps\' Wi-Fi Direct settings. This saves the helper\'s targets; it does not rename either phone. Phone-based controllers only, not Control Hub hotspots.
SAVE NAMES
Enter a name of 1 to 32 UTF-8 bytes, without control characters.
The DS and RC names must be different.
Device names saved. No Wi-Fi reset started.
Android could not save the device names. Try again.
WHAT\'S WRONG?
Checking this phone and the current FTC link.
Connection check finished. No link was reset.
This check does not disconnect, pair, rename, or control the robot. It cannot read the Driver Station\'s FTC handshake status.
DS reported name: %1$s\nExpected: %2$s\nRC target: %3$s
not available
DS NAME MISMATCH\nCorrect Device Names or the FTC phone name first. Do not reset the RC just for this mismatch.

NO WI-FI DIRECT LINK\nTry Fix Connection on the DS while parked. On %1$s, check Wi-Fi is on, keep it unlocked, open Robot Controller, and accept pairing if asked. If a DS fix repeatedly fails, restart the RC app with a mentor; an RC Wi-Fi reset or reboot may help next. This phone cannot prove the RC needs a reset.

DIFFERENT OR UNIDENTIFIED LINK\nThe current group owner is %1$s, not the saved RC target. Check Device Names and FTC pairing with a mentor. This check left the link alone and did not contact that controller.
DS OWNS THE LINK\nThe RC phone should own the FTC Wi-Fi Direct link. Try Fix Connection on the parked DS first. If this repeats, restart the RC app; resetting RC Wi-Fi may help with a mentor.

FTC LINK NOT READY\nThe saved RC is the group owner, but Android has not reported a formed link at 192.168.49.1. Retry after pairing settles, then use the parked DS fix. Repeated failures may need RC-side Wi-Fi recovery.

RC APP RESPONDED\nThe Wi-Fi Direct link and %1$s web service respond. An RC reset is not indicated by this check. Open Driver Station and check its connection status. If it still says disconnected, the FTC handshake may be stuck: try the parked DS fix first, then restart the RC app with a mentor if needed.

RC-SIDE CHECK NEEDED\n%1$s\nOpen Robot Controller on %2$s and retry. If it remains unresponsive, restart that app with the robot parked. If still stuck, reset RC Wi-Fi or reboot with a mentor. A timeout can also mean a routing or link problem; it does not prove the RC app crashed.
WRONG RC IDENTITY\nThe responding controller did not identify itself as %1$s. Check the saved names and FTC pairing before resetting anything.
The RC web service returned HTTP %1$d.
The RC web service could not be reached (%1$s).
The RC web service returned an unreadable identity response.
The RC web service reports it is not alive.
Android did not finish the connection check. Reopen the helper and retry. This is not evidence that the RC needs a reset.
The Wi-Fi Direct link changed during this check. Tap What\'s Wrong again once it settles. This result does not indicate an RC reset is needed.
DS WI-FI IS OFF\nTurn on this phone\'s Wi-Fi using Wi-Fi Controls, then check again. An RC reset is not indicated by this result.
DRIVER STATION UNAVAILABLE\nThe FTC Driver Station app is not installed or its launcher is disabled on this phone. Ask a mentor before changing the RC.
DS WI-FI DIRECT UNAVAILABLE\nReopen this helper. If this phone does not support Wi-Fi Direct, it cannot use this phone-controller helper. This does not diagnose the RC.
DS LOCATION IS OFF\nThis Android version requires Location on to inspect Wi-Fi Direct. Enable Location in Android Settings, then check again.
FIX CONNECTION
OPEN DRIVER STATION
WI-FI CONTROLS
Park and stop the robot, then tap Fix Connection.
Fix Connection resets the FTC Wi-Fi Direct link. This helper never presses INIT or START, changes robot code, or drives the robot.
Is the robot parked and stopped?
The Driver Station will briefly disconnect from %1$s. Use this only while the robot is safely stationary, not during a match.
YES, FIX CONNECTION
Helper reopened. No reset started automatically. Park the robot before retrying.
Allow Nearby devices when asked. Keep both phones unlocked with the Robot Controller app open. Android may ask you to accept pairing on the robot phone.

Wi-Fi Direct permission is required (Nearby devices on Android 13+, Location on older phones). Tap What\'s Wrong or Fix Connection to allow it, or enable it in App Permissions. This does not indicate an RC fault.
APP PERMISSIONS
Allow nearby-device access to find the FTC controller.
